newsitem.title: USA: Morgan, daughter back in U.S. - report.
newsitem.headline: Morgan, daughter back in U.S. - report.

text.p: Elizabeth Morgan, who went to jail and then to New Zealand to keep her ex-husband away from their daughter, has returned to the United States with the child, now 14, the Washington Post reported on Tuesday.
The case was one of the most publicised sexual abuse cases in U.S. history and several books have been written about the saga.

Morgan has accused her ex-husband, Eric Foretich, an oral surgeon, of sexually abusing their daughter from the age of 2, but a judge ruled there was not enough evidence to support the allegation and found Morgan in contempt of court for refusing to comply with his visitation orders.

An attorney for Foretich said he had confirmed through the New Zealand courts that Morgan and her daughter, Ellen -- who was once known as Hillary Foretich -- had come back the United States, and he told the paper he believed the two were now living in the Washington area.
Morgan has remarried and her husband Paul Michel is an appellate judge in Washington. Michel declined comment on his family's whereabouts, calling it "a family matter."
Foretich is challenging a law passed by Congress last year that stripped control of Morgan's case from U.S. courts.

Morgan spent 25 months in jail rather than reveal her child's whereabouts and comply with Foretich's visitation rights. She was released in 1989 after Congress passed a law freeing her. She then joined her daughter, who was living with Morgan's parents in New Zealand.

Morgan and Foretich have been battling in the courts for 15 years. Morgan has a legion of supporters who see her as a heroine for shielding her daughter from Foretich, but Foretich claims she is mentally ill.
Foretich's attorney told the newspaper his client would not be seek custody or renew his quest for visitation rights.
